q.t: The living components of a habitat are…
q.e: Plants, animals, microorganisms.

q.t: Which is abiotic?
q.e: Air, water, soil, sunlight, temperature.

q.t: A group of the same type of organism in a habitat is a…
q.e: E.g. all fish of one kind in a pond.

q.t: Different populations sharing a habitat form a…
q.e: All the plants, animals and microbes together.

q.t: A community plus the abiotic components is an…
q.e: All interacting.

q.t: Green plants are…
q.e: They make their own food.

q.t: Fungi and bacteria that feed on dead matter are…
q.e: Sapro = rotten.

q.t: A deer is a…
q.e: Eats only plants.

q.t: A crow is an…
q.e: Eats both plants and animals.

q.t: Interconnected food chains form a…
q.e: More realistic than a single chain.

q.t: Honeybee and flower — both benefit. This is…
q.e: Bee gets nectar; flower gets pollinated.

q.t: Orchid on a tree — orchid benefits, tree unaffected. This is…
q.e: One benefits, the other is unaffected.

q.t: Tick on a dog is…
q.e: One benefits, the other is harmed.

q.t: Why do elephants enter villages?
o: Their forest habitats have shrunk or changed
q.e: Corridors help them travel safely.

q.t: An ecosystem is ___ a community.
q.e: Ecosystem > community > population.

q.t: In a crop field pyramid, which is most numerous?
q.e: Most at the base, fewest at the top.

q.t: Why does a number pyramid narrow upwards?
o: Many lower organisms are needed to feed one above
q.e: Each level supports fewer individuals.

q.t: Plants affect abiotic components by…
q.e: Dependence runs both ways.

q.t: The world's largest mangrove forest is…
q.e: Between India and Bangladesh.

q.t: Decomposition is important because it…
q.e: In nature, nothing is wasted.

q.t: In the fish-and-flowers study, the pond with fish had…
o: Fewer dragonflies, more pollinators, more seeds
q.e: Fish eat dragonfly larvae; dragonflies eat pollinators.

q.t: Overfishing a pond would likely…
o: Raise dragonflies, cut pollinators, lower seed production
q.e: An indirect effect through three steps.

q.t: A day-active rodent and a night-active snake share a forest. This shows…
o: Organisms coexist by using resources differently
q.e: Same place, different conditions and times.

q.t: If all decomposers disappeared…
o: Dead matter would pile up and soil would lose fertility
q.e: Nutrients would stay locked in dead matter.

q.t: India banned frog leg export because…
o: Fewer frogs led to more insect pests
q.e: Frogs eat insects; removing them upset the balance.

q.t: Why is a food web more resilient than a single chain?
o: Predators with several food sources can switch
q.e: One prey vanishing doesn't doom them.

q.t: Ecosystem balance is…
q.e: It can be disrupted by natural or human changes.

q.t: Competition in an ecosystem…
o: Controls population size and keeps balance
q.e: Prevents one species multiplying too far.

q.t: Overuse of pesticides eventually raises pest numbers because…
o: It kills natural predators of pests
q.e: Some pests also develop resistance.

q.t: Monoculture harms because it…
q.e: Growing one crop repeatedly degrades soil.

q.t: Arrange trophic levels: tiger, grass, deer.
q.e: Producer → herbivore → carnivore.

q.t: A fish gets food (biotic) from small organisms and oxygen (abiotic) from…
q.e: A habitat supplies both kinds of needs.

q.t: What would happen if a habitat had only one type of organism?
q.e: All would need the same resources.

q.t: Mangroves protect coastal villages from tsunamis by…
o: Slowing water and breaking wave force
q.e: Villages behind intact mangroves suffer less.

q.t: Why are synthetic fertilisers overused a problem?
o: They reduce soil microbes and humus, causing erosion
q.e: Without humus the soil doesn't bind.

q.t: Vrikshayurveda advocates nourishing soil with…
q.e: An ancient emphasis on soil health.

q.t: Migratory birds help ecosystems by…
o: Pollinating and dispersing seeds along their routes
q.e: They link habitats far apart.

q.t: A.J.T. Johnsingh pioneered…
q.e: His work in Bandipur studied wildlife movement.

q.t: Human-made ecosystems like farms differ from natural ones because they…
q.e: Unlike natural ecosystems they don't sustain themselves.

q.t: Which pair is matched correctly?
q.e: Shikra is a bird of prey.
